questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Greece?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Greece article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Greece?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Greece on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Greece article.

questions.proof: It borders Albania, North Macedonia and Bulgaria to the north, and Turkey to the east.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Greece?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Greece article.

questions.proof: This is why other languages use many Greek words.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Greece?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Greece article.

questions.proof: Greece, officially the Hellenic Republic, historically known as Hellas, is a country mostly located in Southeastern Europe with small island territories in Asia.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The official language spoken in Greece is Greek, spoken by 99% of the population, and by 90% of the population of the Republic of _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Republic”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Greece article.

questions.proof: The official language spoken in Greece is Greek, spoken by 99% of the population, and by 90% of the population of the Republic of Cyprus.
